events.text: Built the proof: paint_on_3d_demo is now FILLABLE. Drag on the model paints cells into a paint-layer set (raycast pick per cell); each painted cell renders as ONE solid Graph.Path polygon from its projected face corners. Adjacent cells share exact projected corners so the fills tile seamlessly — a continuous layer with no per-row boxes and no fractional-rounding gaps, hence NO pinstripes (the contrast with the old paintRuns row-boxes baked into the atlas). The auto-orbit camera freezes while a stroke is held so the target holds still; the grid stays uniform model-space; fills clip per-face. Verified with a seeded block (top face, cu2..6 x cv0..4): a solid red region, seamless, clipped exactly at the face edge — no banding. Commit b1d5041a6.

resolution: Diagnosed the paint 'pinstripes' artifact and laid out the fix plan. Root cause is in TextureAtlas.tsx:130: paint cells are merged by paintRuns into one horizontal run-box PER ROW and rasterized into the offscreen atlas at top=r.y*tpx, height=max(1,tpx). tpx (atlas-pixels per paint cell) is almost always fractional, and each row-box's top and height round to device pixels independently, so row y's bottom rarely meets row y+1's top — periodically a 1px gap opens, the layer beneath shows through, and the periodic error reads as evenly-spaced horizontal pinstripes (runs merge along x, so columns stay seamless — hence horizontal-only). Plan: stop rasterizing paint as boxes baked into the packed atlas; make paint a CONTINUOUS layer — either a real GPU paint texture (paintable.zig brush passes, like paintable_demo) or an analytic per-fragment composite (like triangle_mask_demo), composited as base_atlas + paint_layer in the mesh shader with the atlas left read-only. A GPU/shader fill has no rows, so no gap, so no stripes — and the same single change also retires the slivers (uniform model-space grid) and the spill (per-pixel face mask). Stopgap if the box approach must ship today: set each row box height = round((y+1)*tpx) - round(y*tpx) so each box's bottom equals the next box's top (gap impossible). Recommended the continuous-layer fix. No code committed yet — offered to prove it by making paint_on_3d_demo fillable (solid stripe-free fill compositing over the untouched material); awaiting go-ahead.
